name: Florian Pfisterer
headline:
Improving medical diagnostics in hemato-oncology with machine learning.
AI Researcher | AI/ML Engineer | PhD Statistics@LMU
summary:
I’m a senior Machine Learning & AI Lead working and innovating at the intersection of data science, automation, and clinical diagnostics. 
I currently lead a team of senior AI engineers and co-design the AI roadmap focused on blood cancer diagnostics. Before that, I worked on building AI solutions that help flow cytometry experts to come to faster and more accurate diagnoses. 

With a strong foundation in ML, statistics, and software engineering, I design and scale end-to-end AI systems - from clinical-grade data pipelines, leveraging the latest trends in AI research to solve clinical problems and GenAI empowered data enrichment and automation workflows.
My work helps make internal clinical data ingestion more fluid, supports faster diagnostic decision-making, and contributes to regulatory and IVDR-aligned AI product development.

I’m particularly interested in:
- Building robust ML/LLM pipelines aligned with business and clinical KPIs
- Creating tools and infrastructure that accelerate productisation and learning cycles
- Integrating AI development with MLOps, 

In the past, I have worked in a variety of roles, some examples include: 
- In my current job, I wrangle data, think about, design and build machine learning pipelines that support diagnosticians with blood cancer diagnosis.
- As a researcher, I led and executed several research projects in AutoML, Algorithmic Fairness, and Domain Generalisation, leading to new insights for practitioners in the field of ML.
- As a freelancer, I taught courses on programming, data science and machine learning/deep learning at large companies in Germany and consulted on projects in the data science / AI realm.
- I am a core developer of several machine learning software packages, mostly in R and Python.

Excited about opportunities where I get to turn data into products and actionable insights.
